title: Google_Research
summary:
Google Research (also known as Research at Google) is the research division of Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. Its mission is to drive breakthroughs that benefit society, businesses, and Google products. Through foundational work in machine learning and generative AI, they deliver broad applications and transformative impact across many domains such as science, healthcare, climate, education, and more. They advance scientific progress by publishing hundreds of papers each year and collaborating with universities, NGOs, partners, and communities worldwide.

Google Research includes the former Google Brain team, a deep learning artificial intelligence research group that served as the sole AI branch of Google before being incorporated under the newer umbrella of Google AI. Google Brain was formed in 2011, combined open-ended machine learning research with information systems and large-scale computing resources, and created tools such as TensorFlow. In April 2023, Google Brain was merged into former Google sister company DeepMind to form Google DeepMind.

Google Research is based in Mountain View, California, and has satellite groups in Accra, Amsterdam, Atlanta, Beijing, Berlin, Cambridge (Massachusetts), Israel, Los Angeles, London, Montreal, Munich, New York City, Paris, Pittsburgh, Princeton, San Francisco, Seattle, Tokyo, Toronto, and Zurich. Google began in January 1996 as a research project by Larry Page and Sergey Brin while they were both PhD students at Stanford University.

In September 2025, Google opened their 735 million pound AI Centre in Waltham Cross, Hertfordshire, and announced plans for 5 billion pounds of investment in AI research. The division continues to focus on areas ranging from foundational AI research to applied science, working to integrate research findings directly into Google's products and services.
